title: Is This the Kind Return
description: Is This the Kind Return in Tonic Solfa to BOYLSTON, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 6 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for his Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707), Book II, composed on divine subjects, hymn 74, headed “Repentance from a sense of divine goodness; or, A complaint of ingratitude”.
Watts' hymns were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Short Metre (6.6.8.6). This page sets the words to BOYLSTON; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Is this the kind re-turn, And these the thanks we owe, Thus to a-buse e-ter-nal love, Whence all our bless-ings flow?

lines: And these the thanks we owe,
On us he bids the sun
For us the skies their circles run
And bow their necks to men,
But we more base, more brutish things
Break, sovereign grace, these hearts of stone,
And give us hearts of flesh.
And hourly as new mercies fall

source: Isaac Watts, Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to BOYLSTON by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
